answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent identity to a small, time-locked stake held in a shared vault: before an agent can act, it deposits collateral that only unlocks after a cooling period of honest work. A wharf-style registry then checks that stake against a live pulse of recent behavior, so a single operator spinning up thousands of sock-puppet agents must fund every identity separately, and bad behavior forfeits the deposit. Sybils become expensive to mint and cheap to punish, while legitimate agents keep working uninterrupted.
